correctness.rationale: For a single circle of length a, intrinsic distance of two uniform points is uniform on [0,a/2], producing same-circle ordered pair tail J_c(a)=a(a-c)_+. For distinct petals the junction distances are independent uniforms on [0,a/2],[0,b/2], giving K_c(a,b)=ab-[c²-(c-a)_+²-(c-b)_+²+(c-a-b)_+²]/2. Summing over petals yields exact full tail. Increasing a>b and decreasing b has two-petal derivative c*1_{b<c<a}, while each third petal contributes 2(partial_a K_c(a,d)-partial_b K_c(b,d))>=0, since partial_xK=d-(c-x)_++(c-x-d)_+ is increasing in x. Continuity across hinges and the finite Robin Hood transfer characterization give all-length, all-threshold majorization. Taking c between a,b yields strictness over an interval; at small thresholds the common 1-2t/L-2m(m-1)t²/L² plateau prevents an over-strong pointwise strictness claim. Independently tested exact rational sums for random transfers m2..7 and all hinge boundaries, corroborative but not proof.

value.rationale: A full first-order stochastic order simultaneously controls every increasing risk functional and all quantiles of geodesic distance, strictly strengthening the known mean-minimization classification on a canonical family of compact metric graphs. The explicit tail kernels, all-threshold derivative and sharp non-strict near-zero plateau are structural, independently useful geometric probability facts.

final_claim: For bouquets of m>=2 positive-length metric circles with fixed total length, majorization of petal lengths increases the full survival law of intrinsic distances of two independent uniform-arclength points. Distinct length multisets have strictly different laws, with a nonempty threshold interval of strict inequality; the equilateral flower is uniquely stochastically minimal.
limitations: Fixed flower topology of positive loops, fixed total arclength, independent arclength-uniform endpoints and intrinsic metric only.
Strict comparison holds on an interval, NOT every positive threshold; common near-zero tail and far-zero tails are essential.
